correctness.rationale: The direction-indexed Mittag-Leffler Laplace transforms j lambda/(j lambda+s^alpha) and j mu/(j mu+s^alpha) are realized as stable subordinators evaluated at independent exponentials of linearly increasing rates. Sums of those exponentials equal exponential maxima G_m/lambda and G_k/mu. The stable-ratio integration identity E[U/(U+V)]=a/(a+b) proves exact finite-count alpha-independent mean, including one-side-empty cases. Uniform log expansion of the product transforms gives joint independent stable limits when beta_±=lim log(1+np_±)/log n exist; max beta=1 ensures ratio continuity. The Lamperti density follows by Stieltjes inversion, and a two-variable Taylor expansion around L=log n using bounded second moments of G_m-log n proves the fixed-p log-odds bias coefficient lambda mu/(lambda+mu)^2*log(p/(1-p))/L with O(L^-2). Independently computed exact rational two-direction fractional Laplace factors for n=1,5,15 to check the operational-time mixture. These finite checks do not prove the limits; proof covers all stated alpha,p_n under the explicit exponent assumption.
